mutations.why: This restores the exact defect of the sprint, in the new shape: an unreachable origin reported as 'the branch is not on the remote'. It is the one-line difference between the fix and the bug, and before this sprint nothing in the suite could tell them apart.
mutations.label: finish-sprint:ls-remote-failure-is-not-absence
mutations.expectRed: an ls-remote failure with an origin configured is NOT

mutations.why: Dropping the status check makes every config failure read as 'no origin', rebuilding the swallow one level down in the very function added to remove it. A corrupt config or a non-repo cwd would silently skip the remote delete again.
mutations.label: finish-sprint:origin-probe-discriminates-status
mutations.expectRed: must propagate, not be read as

mutations.why: The exit code is the whole difference between a finish that lied and one that did not. A human reading the console might notice the error text; a script wrapping finish-sprint.js reads only the code.
mutations.find: process.exitCode = 1; // a branch left on the remote is not a successful finish
mutations.label: finish-sprint:leftover-remote-exits-nonzero
mutations.expectRed: a remote branch left behind is not a successful finish

mutations.why: Per-branch isolation that swallows the reason is how debris survives in the first place - the audit would print a confident 'none' for a branch it never managed to judge. The bucket must be visible, not merely non-fatal.
mutations.label: gh-hygiene:unjudged-branch-is-reported
